scenes.heading: Configuring Technical Account Permissions
scenes.narration: Authentication. Configuring Technical Account Permissions. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Does obtaining a valid access token automatically grant access to content or actions in AEM?
scenes.heading: No — a valid access token grants identity, not permissions; the technical account still needs AEM group membership
scenes.body: A valid access token alone does not equal access — it equals identity. The technical account behind that token still needs explicit permissions in AEM, governed by AEM's normal group-and-ACL model, same as any other user.

scenes.question: When does the technical account's corresponding AEM user actually get created?
scenes.heading: After the first API call made with the token, which auto-creates the matching AEM user
scenes.body: The technical account AEM user doesn't exist until the first HTTP request is made using its access token. That first call auto-creates the matching AEM user, after which its permissions can be managed like any other AEM user.

scenes.question: How do you identify the AEM login name of a technical account?
scenes.heading: The integration.email value in the credential JSON — a login name like a UUID at techacct.adobe.com
scenes.body: The Service Credentials JSON includes an integration.email value, which represents the technical account's AEM login name — typically a long UUID-style identifier at the techacct.adobe.com domain.

scenes.question: Where in AEM does an Administrator assign group membership to a technical account user?
scenes.heading: Tools > Security > Users, then finding the user by its technical account login name
scenes.body: An AEM Administrator navigates to Tools > Security > Users, locates the technical account user by its login name (the integration.email value), and adds it to the appropriate group from its Properties.

scenes.question: Which AEM group would you add a technical account to for write access to digital assets?
scenes.heading: The DAM Users group
scenes.body: To grant write access to assets — for example, updating metadata via the Assets HTTP API — the technical account user is added to the DAM Users group, the same as it would be for a human user needing that same access.

scenes.question: What group is a Service Credentials-derived access token's technical account typically assigned to by default?
scenes.heading: The Contributors group, by default, for the technical account behind the local development token
scenes.body: The Service Credentials-derived access token is associated with a technical account AEM user, typically assigned membership in the Contributors AEM user group by default, granting the baseline permissions needed to interact with AEM.

scenes.question: Once created, does a technical account AEM user follow the same permission model as a human user?
scenes.heading: Yes — its permissions are governed entirely by its group memberships, exactly like a human user's
scenes.body: Once the technical account AEM user exists, its permissions can be managed exactly like any other AEM user's — through group membership and ACLs. There's no separate, special permission model for machine identities.

scenes.question: How do you verify that a technical account's API request actually applied a permission-dependent change, like a metadata update?
scenes.heading: Reviewing the Advanced tab of an asset's Properties and checking the updated metadata value against what the request set
scenes.body: To verify a change made via a technical account's access token — for example an updated dc:rights metadata property — log into the AEM environment, navigate to the asset, open its Properties, go to the Advanced tab, and confirm the value matches what the request specified.
